<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 32%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>BM&#038;F BOVESPA: VALE3, VALE5<BR>
NYSE: VALE, VALE.P<BR>
HKEx: 6210, 6230<BR>
EURONEXT PARIS: VALE3, VALE5<BR>
LATIBEX: XVALO, XVALP</B>

</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 68%">

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>A YEAR OF EXTRAORDINARY PERFORMANCE</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><IMG src="c13242c1324202.gif" alt="(GRAPHIC)">

</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Performance of Vale in 2010</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Rio de Janeiro, February&nbsp;24, 2011 &#151; Vale S.A. (Vale) reports a stellar performance in 4Q10
and 2010. It is our best ever annual result, characterized by all-time high figures for operating
revenues, operating income, operating margin, cash generation and net earnings. Net earnings for
2010 were the greatest ever in the mining industry. At the same time, we allocated the greatest
amount of resources in the global mining industry to fund the creation of new platforms for future
growth to sustain high performance.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Roger Agnelli, our Chief Executive Officer, has commented: &#147;We are living through our best days.
However, given the size and quality of our pipeline of growth projects amid a scenario of sustained
global demand growth for our products, I strongly believe that even better days are ahead of us&#148;.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">2009 was a transition year, marked by weaker but still robust performance. 2010 was a year of
strong recovery and striking performance due to the combination of two powerful forces. On the one
hand, the initiatives developed by the company in response to the global economic downturn,
embracing change and structural transformation, began to bear fruits. On the other hand, the global
economy, led by emerging economies, the main drivers of the demand for minerals and metals, showed
an above-trend growth, rallying from the depressed levels of late 2008/early 2009.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>
<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 32%">

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>www.vale.com<BR>
rio@vale.com</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="Center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Departament of<BR>
Investor Relations</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="Center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Roberto Castello Branco<BR>
Viktor Moszkowicz<BR>
Carla Albano Miller<BR>
Andrea Gutman<BR>
Christian Perlingiere<BR>
Fernando Frey<BR>
Marcio Loures Penna<BR>
Samantha Pons<BR>
Thomaz Freire<BR>
Tel: (5521)&nbsp;3814-4540
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 68%">

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our powerful cash generation and rigorous discipline in capital allocation allowed us to
overcome once again the challenge posed to growth companies by the classical trilemma involving
growth financing, soundness of the balance sheet and meeting shareholders&#146; aspirations for capital
return.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale has invested US$12.7&nbsp;billion in maintenance of existing assets and the exploitation of
multiple organic growth opportunities. Six projects were delivered in 2010: (a)&nbsp;Additional 20 Mtpy,
an iron ore expansion of Caraj&#225;s operations; (b)&nbsp;TKCSA, a steel slab plant; (c)&nbsp;Bay&#243;var, a
phosphate rock mine; (d)&nbsp;Tres Valles, a copper operation; (e)&nbsp;On&#231;a Puma, a ferronickel operation;
and (f)&nbsp;Oman, an iron ore pellet operation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Moreover, we spent US$6.7&nbsp;billion to finance acquisitions, including fertilizer assets in Brazil.
In total, Vale&#146;s investment in 2010 reached US$19.4&nbsp;billion, the largest in the world&#146;s mining
industry.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Simultaneously, we have returned US$5.0&nbsp;billion to shareholders, a record amount, being US$3.0
billion of dividend distribution and US$2.0&nbsp;billion through a share buyback. In addition, an
extraordinary dividend of US$1&nbsp;billion was distributed to shareholders on January&nbsp;31, 2011.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>4Q10</B>
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->1<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">



<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 32%">

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><I><B>US GAAP</B></I>
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 68%">

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">After spending almost US$25&nbsp;billion with investments and cash returns to shareholders, we were able
to deleverage the balance sheet, ending the year with a total debt/adjusted EBITDA ratio of 1.0x.
</DIV>










<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In December&nbsp;2010, our shares were listed for trading on the Main Board of The Stock Exchange
of Hong Kong Limited (HKEx). With the listing in one of the most important stock exchanges in Asia,
we offer now to investors all over the world the option of trading our shares around the clock, in
the Americas, Europe and Asia, consolidating Vale&#146;s position as a major global company.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Over the last ten years, Vale created US$154.5&nbsp;billion of value to shareholders and distributed
US$17.4&nbsp;billion in dividends. Total shareholder return was 38.2% per annum for 2001-2010, the
highest among our peers.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">As an agent of global sustainability, we invested US$737&nbsp;million in environmental protection and
conservation and US$399&nbsp;million in social projects, totaling expenditures of US$1.136&nbsp;billion in
corporate social responsibility. We continued to develop technological solutions to reconcile
excellence in operational and financial performance with sustainability, creating opportunities for
social and economic mobility for the communities where we have our operations.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The main highlights of Vale&#146;s performance were:
</DIV>

4Q10, an all-time high figure in a fourth quarter.</DIV></TD>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>
<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<TR style="font-size: 1px">
    <TD align="right" valign="top" style="border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;
</TD>

<TD nowrap colspan="2" align="center" valign="top" style="border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"> <B>BUSINESS OUTLOOK</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The world economy is accelerating faster than anticipated and 2011 is likely to be another
year of growth above the long-term trend of 4% per annum.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">After a mid-year soft patch, global manufacturing output reaccelerated in 4Q10 and continued to
expand in the beginning of this year, suggesting that the pace of inventory building has fallen
significantly and companies are responding to a stronger final demand for goods. After dropping
from April to September last year, for January&nbsp;2011 the JP Morgan Global Manufacturing PMI showed
the fourth month of sequential increase. Simultaneously, the new orders index and the
orders/inventory ratio &#151; two important leading indicators &#151; are rising and returning to the levels
prevailing in 1Q10, thereby signaling increases in industrial production over the next few months.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Given the dynamics of recoveries from recessions, we do not expect the return to the two-digit
manufacturing output growth seen in the first twelve months of the global recovery, but a robust
expansion supportive of a strong demand for minerals and metals.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Growth in global economic activity now has more sectorial and geographical breadth than in the
first leg of the recovery from the Great Recession of 2008/2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">For the first time since mid-2003, when global GDP was expanding above 5% per annum, there is a
synchronized acceleration in the manufacturing and services sectors, indicating a broad-based
pickup in final demand which adds strength to growth sustainability. The rebound in services sector
activity is especially important given its potential to generate a powerful job increase, thereby
fueling further consumption expenditures.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Alongside the sectorial broadening of growth, there are improvements in the geographic landscape of
global economic activity. The shift in momentum has become broadly based across countries, which is
an additional force to enhance the recovery. While the US is taking a leading role in global growth
reacceleration, the core countries of the Euro zone seem to be experiencing a solid rebound.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Although there are risks of financial turbulence resurfacing in the periphery of the Euro area, it
is likely that markets will behave in the same way they did during the bout of turbulence in
December&nbsp;2010, when the stresses remained contained without spillovers to other countries. Despite
the potential for closer integration within the Euro zone, peripheral economies usually have
business cycles which are asynchronous to those of the core economies, and we expect this to
continue in the near term.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">A few fundamental forces underlie the continuation of the expansion of global economic activity at
high pace.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Monetary policies remain accommodative in developed economies, where policy interest rates are
negative in real terms, which has been instrumental in sustaining the recovery.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Powered by healthy balance sheets, strong profitability and cash flows, the corporate sector has
shifted from a defensive stance since mid-2010, towards a more aggressive boosting of capital
expenditures. For instance, global mining capex, led by Vale with US$24&nbsp;billion, is very likely to
surpass this year the peak of US$120&nbsp;billion reached in 2008. Spending on consumer durables, which
had remained subdued in developed economies, has been increasing in the US and Japan since late
last year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Financial conditions have been supportive of growth. Simultaneously to the ample liquidity and low
price volatility in global capital markets, on the bank credit side Senior Lending Officer surveys
for the US, Japan, the Euro zone and the UK are showing a marked improvement in both supply (credit
terms and standards) and demand for corporate loans, which generates a positive feedback loop to
economic recovery. For the first time since 3Q07 the surveys are indicating growth in the demand
for credit, which has been more pronounced in the US and Germany. At the same time, banks have
moved to begin easing terms and lending standards for credit to consumers, including credit cards
and auto loans, while consumer demand has stabilized after a long period of weakening since 2006.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Over the last few months, flows of investor funds have been reallocated from emerging to developed
markets. As a consequence, equity prices in emerging markets have been underperforming those in developed markets notably in the first months of 2011.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->5<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">


<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<TR style="font-size: 1px">
    <TD align="right" valign="top" style="border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;
</TD>

<TD nowrap colspan="2" align="center" valign="top" style="border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">This movement is partly influenced by the change in sentiment about the growth prospects of
developed economies, which until recently were bearish. Another reason is investor fear of rising
inflation in emerging economies, as emerging market central banks are seen as being behind the
curve in the tightening cycle.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">As a matter of fact, despite the interconnections provided by globalization, emerging economies are
expected to continue the decoupling from advanced economies, in line with the longer term
phenomenon of conditional convergence of low per capita incomes to the levels achieved by richer
nations.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Faster growth in the developed world, all other things constant, can only boost through several
channels the expansion of emerging economies. Moreover, it helps to strengthen the demand for
minerals and metals in these countries. After a severe contraction in 2009, metals consumption in
the developed world is still below pre-crisis levels. This is more noticeable in the case of steel,
where consumption levels prevailing in 2010 were almost 20% lower than the peak in 2007.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">A significant part of the price pressures comes from the sharp rise in agricultural prices since
mid-2010 caused by the various supply shocks, originating from adverse weather conditions in
countries such as Russia, Australia, Argentina, the US and China. The pass through of food prices
to headline inflation rates tends to be much higher in emerging economies, which are more intensive
consumers of non-processed food and where a larger share of household budgets is dedicated to food
consumption.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Food price hikes represent relative price changes &#151; food is becoming more expensive relative to
other goods and services &#151; and are not a fundamental cause of inflation &#151; a generalized and
continuous price increase. Thus, they tend to imply only a temporary rise in headline inflation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The influence of commodity prices on consumer price indices tends to be weak, with their impact
being diluted throughout the production chain, decreasing its magnitude as one move from the
upstream to the downstream. Since the 80&#146;s, when central banks began to gain credibility as
inflation fighters, there has been very low correlation between changes in commodity prices and
core consumer prices, even in periods when economic growth and resource utilization was high.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Central bankers in emerging markets are responding accordingly to the agricultural price shocks by
lifting policy interest rates to contain their second-order effects, a preemptive step taken to
block the transmission of these to other prices in the economy which could affect core inflation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">There are a few cases of emerging countries where excess demand is underlying the changes in
inflationary expectations. In these cases, central banks are tightening monetary policy alongside a
firmer normalization of fiscal policies from the countercyclical stance adopted during 2009 to
forestall the recessionary pressures stemming from the global financial shock.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The major challenge ahead is to normalize policy at a speed that sustains growth while restraining
the buildup of inflationary pressures that will emerge as the expansionary cycle matures. The
experience of monetary policy making in emerging economies over at least the last ten years tells
us that central banks had managed to overcome this challenge. And the credibility of monetary
policy in emerging economies is one of the factors that have contributed to their resilience in the
face of the global financial crisis and their faster economic growth over the last decade.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">We believe that, unless underlying conditions deteriorate, these fears are similar to other noises
that in the recent past were able to produce spikes of financial asset and commodity price
volatility with no impact on the real economy and/or the economic growth outlook.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the specific case of China, the largest emerging market economy, the recent hikes in consumer
price indices have given rise to increasing concerns with inflation and the consequences of
inflation fighting. The higher monthly inflation rates have come mostly from food prices, with
weather-sensitive vegetable prices leading the way. While food inflation &#151; food represents 34% of
the CPI basket &#151; is running at 10.3% on a year-on-year basis, non-food prices have increased by
2.6%. Assuming no unusual major natural disasters, we expect food prices to moderate later
contributing to slow inflation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The People&#146;s Bank of China (PBoC), China&#146;s central bank, uses several tools to control money and
credit, with the later being a very important variable as it amounts to some 130% of GDP. Although
there are other sources of financing, bank lending remains the most important source of external financing for companies and local governments.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->6<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">



<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>

    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>

<TR style="font-size: 1px">
    <TD align="right" valign="top" style="border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;

<TD nowrap colspan="2" align="center" valign="top" style="border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The PBoC has raised banks&#146; required reserve ratios by eight times since the beginning of last year
in order to mop up liquidity, in an effort to sterilize the monetary impact of the large increases
in the country&#146;s stock of international reserves, at costs lower than market interest rates.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Bank lending rates are directly set by the PBoC and they really matter for the cost of capital.
Given their systematic low level in real terms, especially when compared to expected returns on
fixed asset investment, they have not been the binding constraint for the demand for loans. By the
same token, we believe that raising rates at the margin does not affect the amount of bank
borrowing.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Unless the PBoC decides to use more market oriented tools, producing, for instance, a major
interest rate hike, the most effective instrument for controlling credit expansion is the
employment of direct quantitative controls, which works by obliging the large state-owned
commercial banks to slow down lending, as it happened in 2004, at the end of 2007 and during part
of 2008.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">So far during this cycle, Chinese authorities have not employed quantitative controls to restrain
commercial bank credit expansion, which is believed to be due to the expectations that the current
inflation rate increases are a temporary phenomenon.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Industrial output and fixed asset investment in China reaccelerated in the second half of 2010. As
measured by GDP growth, the Chinese economy performed very well in the last quarter of 2010, with
an expansion of 12% on a quarter-on-quarter seasonally annualized adjusted basis, the highest
increase since 2Q09, when it was recovering from the global financial shock.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">We expect China&#146;s growth to remain above 10% during the first half of 2011, mainly driven by
domestic demand, with a softening in the second semester. The demand for minerals and metals is
expected to remain strong not only due to rapid economic growth but also to restocking.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Since mid-July&nbsp;2010 iron ore prices in the spot market have been increasing, reaching almost US$200
per metric ton, thus surpassing the peak level of the post-crisis period, at US$186 in April last
year. Rising prices are reflecting a combination of a strong Chinese-led global demand and a tight
supply.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Global carbon steel output followed a path very similar to the one taken by global industrial
production. After a strong recovery since mid-2009 it peaked in April&nbsp;2010 and then started to
weaken. A reversal trend was set in motion in 4Q10 and last December steel output reached a new
all-time high, at 1.47&nbsp;billion metric tons, on a seasonally adjusted annualized basis, which
translated into increasing demand pressure for iron ore and metallurgical coal.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">On the supply side, India, until a few years ago the second largest supplier to China, has lost
ground, being surpassed by Brazil since 2007. Its market share in Chinese imports has declined
continuously since 2005, to 15.6% in 2010 from a peak of 25% attained in 2005.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">India has been reallocating an increasing amount of iron ore to its blast furnaces, given the
strong demand for steel arising from a fast growing economy, which stimulated steel output to
expand at an average annual rate of 11.7% between 2005 and 2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Therefore, last year&#146;s fall in Indian exports by 11%, the first in many years, is hardly a one-off
event and is more likely part of a trend, as India will need an increasing volume of iron ore to
support its industrialization process and the badly needed large investments in infrastructure
building.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The quality of Chinese iron ore has been deteriorating continuously, requiring an increasing amount
of run-of-the-mine to produce iron ore to be used in blast furnaces and failing to accelerate
production as envisaged. A clear indication of the tightness in the global supply of iron ore is
the fact that in order to meet its growing demand for imports China has been widening its base of
suppliers, adding small scale non-traditional suppliers as well as overland suppliers, since the
traditional seaborne suppliers &#151; Brazil, Australia and India &#151; have not been able to satisfy its
appetite for the raw material.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Metallurgical coal prices have been increasing since 2H10 due to demand pressures and the supply
shock produced by heavy rainfall and floods in the state of Queensland, Australia, a major global
producer and exporter, and tends to stay at high levels, implying a positive spillover to the iron
ore market. More expensive coal tends to stimulate the more intensive use of high quality iron ore to save consumption of coke at the steel mills&#146; blast furnaces, adding pressure to the price
premium for our iron ores.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->7<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Eliminating cyclical influences and short-term price volatility, real iron ore prices seem to be in
an upward long-term trend similar to the one that lasted from World War II to the early seventies.
The trend reflects an increase in the premium for relative scarcity, as despite the price
incentives for production capacity expansion has not been sufficient to keep pace with demand
mostly due to geological and institutional constraints. One fact that is frequently missed when
projecting future production is the extent of the demand of investment for repletion, which
requires relatively large volumes of iron ore just to replace lost capacity.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Amid this scenario of deepening scarcity, Vale&#146;s huge, high quality reserves of iron ore and its
proven capacity to develop and deliver large-scale projects supported by a powerful cash flow are a
major competitive edge and contributor to shareholder value creation<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP>.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Following three years of decline, global stainless steel production &#151; responsible for almost two
thirds of primary nickel consumption &#151; surged in 2010, increasing by 23.4%, an all-time high pace
of growth. After a quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted annual expansion of 10% in 4Q10,
stainless steel production has strengthened further as many mills are running at full capacity due
to rising orders. Prices for the 304 stainless steel are continuing to rise, with their current
levels still 30% below the peak reached in 2007.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The demand for nickel from non-stainless steel applications, a market in which Vale is the leading
player, has been strong and is also gaining momentum, fueled by end-users from the aerospace, oil
and gas and petrochemical industries.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Demand was sufficiently strong to more than offset the pressure on prices coming from production
increases in 2010. For instance, as a result of the normalization of the Canadian operations in
2H10 our nickel production augmented by 55.7% in relation to 1H10. After the correction caused by
the financial stress in Continental Europe in 2Q10, the strong fundamentals and the marginal
influence of commodity price co-movement led nickel prices to climb to almost US$30,000 recently
from US$18,000 per metric ton in early June&nbsp;2010. Nickel stocks, which had gradually increased from
August&nbsp;2010 to yearend due to expectations of higher prices, began to fall after mid-January&nbsp;2011
reflecting disequilibrium between demand and supply.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Nickel fundamentals are expected to remain strong in the foreseeable future.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Stainless steel consumption is strongly correlated to consumption expenditures and is highly
elastic to income growth. This helps to explain why nickel consumption intensity, as measured by
consumption per US$ of GDP, is still lower in emerging economies than in advanced economies,
differently from other metals such as steel and copper. Emerging economies are expected to remain
in the high per capita income growth path and, as in recent years, to drive global consumption
expenditures, suggesting that the demand for nickel has significant growth potential over the
medium term.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the short term, supply is not expected to show a material reaction to prices. One of the two
furnaces of our Copper Cliff smelter in Sudbury will remain shut down for a minimum of 16&nbsp;weeks,
entailing an estimated output loss of 15,000 metric tons of finished nickel. Moreover, production
increases arising from the industry&#146;s new projects coming on stream this year are expected to take
place mostly in 2H11.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Nickel laterite limonite projects &#151; the most abundant type of nickel ores in world resources &#151; are
struggling to live up to expectations in terms of duration of ramp up and achievement of nameplate
capacities. These difficulties have the potential to keep global supply tight for the long-term.
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 10pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>

at 35.7% per year, according to &#147;Value creation in mining&#148;, issued by The
Boston Consulting Group, February&nbsp;2011. From December&nbsp;2008 to December&nbsp;2009
Vale created US $130&nbsp;billion in value for shareholders and distributed US $15.3
billion in dividends.</DIV></TD>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Alongside a strong demand, copper supply constraints continue to exert upward price pressures. In
addition to one-off events, such as labor strikes, the difficulties in maintaining output levels at
older mines &#151; where grades have been declining steadily &#151; are a key feature of the supply
constraint phenomenon. A tight market and at the margin the contribution of commodity price
co-movement have led copper prices to climb to US$10,000 per metric ton early this month,
increasing by 64% over the lows of US$6,100 in early June&nbsp;2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The rising supply of scrap, stimulated by the copper price movement, and the potential threat of
substitution, given the widening of the spread
with aluminum prices &#151; which jumped to US$7,500 in February&nbsp;2011 from US$1,275 per metric ton in
January&nbsp;2009 &#151; are likely to influence some price moderation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">At the moment, Vale is ramping up Tres Valles, a copper project in Chile, with a capacity of 18,500
metric tons per year of copper cathodes. The first phase of Salobo, with a capacity of 100,000
metric tons per year of copper in concentrates, is expected to come on stream in 2H11.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The market for fertilizers is being positively influenced by the rise in farming profitability
determined by the surge in grain prices, favorable financial conditions and inventory consumption
during 2009 and part of last year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Most of our production is destined for the Brazilian market, which is the fourth largest consumer
in the world and where consumption has grown by 6% per annum over the last two decades, far above
global expansion. Demand is seasonally low in the first half of the year, strengthening later to
meet Brazil&#146;s main ploughing season, from September to November.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Prices of phosphate rock and phosphates, such as MAP and DAP, began to rise in early 2010 and are
expected to stay steady over this year. As inventory consumption took a longer period of time,
potash prices started to rebound only late last year and are expected to climb to a higher plateau
in 2011. The positive outlook for the global potash market has been confirmed by the announcements
of price increases in these first two months of the year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Despite the operational and market risks to which mining companies are normally exposed, we expect
the performance of Vale in 2011 to support the sustainability of the shareholder value creation
process.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, our operating revenues achieved a historical high of US$46.481&nbsp;billion, 94.2% above
the US$23.939&nbsp;billion in 2009 and 20.7% higher than our previous record of US$38.509&nbsp;billion in
2008.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Higher prices of products were responsible for 82.1% of the total revenue increase of US$22.542
billion over 2009, contributing with US$18.512&nbsp;billion, while sales volume growth added US$4.030
billion. Higher iron ore and pellet prices were the major contributors, adding US$12.112&nbsp;billion
and US$3.459&nbsp;billion to the revenues, respectively.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, revenues set a new record, at US$15.207&nbsp;billion. It was US$711&nbsp;million higher, 4.9%, than
in 3Q10, which resulted from the contribution of the growth in sales volumes, US$1.030&nbsp;billion.
Lower prices had a negative effect of US$319&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The higher sales volumes were mainly explained by an increase of US$714&nbsp;million in the base metals
business, due to the return to normalcy of the nickel operations in Canada, and US$343&nbsp;million in
the revenues of the bulk materials business. The contraction in prices is mainly due to lower
prices of iron ore and pellets, US$658&nbsp;million, which were partially offset by higher base metals
prices, US$386&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Sales of bulk materials &#151; iron ore, pellets, manganese ore, ferroalloy, metallurgical and thermal
coal &#151; represented 74.2% of the operating revenues in 2010, increasing from 63.7% in 2009. The
share of base metals in total revenues decreased to 17.6% from 27.9% in 2009, due to lower output.
The share of fertilizers was 4.0% in 2010, rising from 1.7% in the previous year. Logistics
services contributed with 3.1% and other products with 1.0%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, sales to Asia represented 53.3% of total revenues, below the participation of 56.9% in
2009. The share of sales to clients in the Americas was 23.6%, in line with the 24.0% for 2009.
Revenues from shipments to Europe increased to 19.2% in 2010 from 16.9% in 2009, recovering part of
the room lost during the economic downturn, while the rest of the world contributed with 3.9%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">On a country basis, China was responsible for 33.1% of our revenues, Brazil 17.5%, Japan 11.3%,
Germany 6.7%, South Korea 4.2%, and Taiwan 2.5%, in 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"> <B>COSTS</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">On the flipside of the strong demand growth and the ensuing rise in prices of minerals and
metals there are demand pressures for labor, equipment, spare parts, engineering services and other
inputs as mining companies are incentivized to run operations at full capacity and to invest in
additional capacity. Therefore, cost pressures are an expected phenomenon during the expansionary
phase of the business cycle.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">This is beginning to happen albeit at a moderate pace. During the last few years we developed
several initiatives to cut costs, with a special focus on fixed costs, to enhance the resilience to
an environment of tight markets for inputs.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our costs in 4Q10 were inflated by the effects of some movements needed to augment the exposure to
the cycle such as the resumption of full capacity operations of the Canadian assets, sales
increases, the consolidation of the newly acquired fertilizers assets and the start-up of projects
coming on stream.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, cost of goods sold (COGS)&nbsp;were up by US$927&nbsp;million on a quarter-on-quarter basis,
reaching US$6.040&nbsp;billion. This increase was primarily due to: (a)&nbsp;additional depreciation charges,
a non-cash item, net of the effect of currency price changes, of US$296&nbsp;million; (b)&nbsp;increase of
purchases of products from third parties, US$232&nbsp;million; (c)&nbsp;additional cost arising from the
resumption of nickel operations, US$228&nbsp;million; (d)&nbsp;depreciation of the US$ dollar, US$118
million<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">2</SUP>; (e)&nbsp;higher sales of other products than nickel, US$77&nbsp;million; (f)&nbsp;costs with
the VNC operations, US$44&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">COGS reached US$18.814&nbsp;billion in 2010, US$5.193&nbsp;billion higher than 2009, impacted by higher sales
of US$1.775&nbsp;billion and exchange rate variation of US$1.323&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 10pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR style="font-size: 6pt">
    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">2</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">COGS currency exposure in 4Q10 was made up as
follow: 64% in Brazilian reais, 17% in US dollars, 14% in Canadian dollars,
1%in Indonesian rupiah and 4% in other currencies.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>



<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="30%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="30%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="30%"></TD>
</TR>

<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom"><!-- Blank Space -->
    <TD align="left" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="center" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="center" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, expenses with energy consumption accounted for 14.3% of COGS. These costs reached
US$861&nbsp;million, in line with US$864&nbsp;million of 3Q10. While costs with fuel and gases at US$484
million declined by 11.0% vis-&#224;-vis 3Q10, those with electricity consumption rose by 17.4%,
reaching US$377&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Expenses with outsourced services totaled US$847&nbsp;million &#151; 14.0% of COGS &#151; against US$722&nbsp;million
in 3Q10. Out of the US$125&nbsp;million increase in costs with these services, US$100&nbsp;million was due to
growth in sales volumes, reflecting mainly the end of labor disruption in our Canadian operations
and the record production level achieved in Caraj&#225;s. The main item of outsourced services was
operational services that reached US$256&nbsp;million, an increase of US$77&nbsp;million, mainly due to ore
and waste removal which rose by US$16&nbsp;million, the remaining US$61&nbsp;million was distributed among
lab, industrial and geological services.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The cost of materials &#151; 13.7% of COGS &#151; was US$826&nbsp;million, with an increase of 12.8% against
3Q10. Excluding effects of higher sales volumes (US$56&nbsp;million) and currency price changes (US$20
million), costs of materials increased by US$17&nbsp;million from last quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Personnel expenses reached US$692&nbsp;million, representing 11.5% of COGS, against US$516&nbsp;million in
3Q10. The increase reflected greater sales volume primarily due to the return to normalcy of our
Canadian operations, US$58&nbsp;million, and exchange rate variation, US$12&nbsp;million. Additionally, in
November&nbsp;2010, Vale&#146;s workers in Brazil received a bonus granted due to the two-year agreement made
in 2009, with a one-off effect of US$32&nbsp;million, and also received a 7% wage increase, adding US$13
million to the personnel costs in 4Q10; hiring of new employees contributed with US$3&nbsp;million and
other factors, such as promotions and payment for extra working hours, with US$29&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The cost of purchasing products from third parties amounted to US$631&nbsp;million &#151; 10.4% of COGS &#151;
against US$399&nbsp;million in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The purchase of iron ore and pellets was US$399&nbsp;million, against US$257&nbsp;million in the previous
quarter, mainly due to increased prices of Hispanobr&#225;s pellets in 4Q10. The volume of iron ore
bought from smaller miners came to 3.1&nbsp;million metric tons (Mt) in 4Q10 compared with 2.3 Mt in
3Q10. The acquisition of pellets from our joint ventures amounted to 620,000 metric tons in this
quarter &#151; against 875,000 metric tons in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Expenditures with the purchase of nickel products rose to US$135&nbsp;million from US$63&nbsp;million in
3Q10. There was a substantial increase in the purchase of intermediate products, partly offset by a
reduction in the acquisition of finished nickel. Both movements are related to the return to
normalcy of our Canadian operations in this quarter. Mining as well as smelting and refining
operations at Sudbury, the precious metals plant of Port Colborne, and Voisey&#146;s Bay mining and
processing operations were ramped up.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Costs with shared services reached US$69&nbsp;million, exactly the same level as in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Due to organic growth and acquisitions our asset base has been expanding: PP&#038;E, net of depreciation
and construction in progress, rose to US$61.337&nbsp;billion in 2010 from US$47.699&nbsp;billion by the end
of 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The costs of depreciation and amortization &#151; 15.3% of COGS &#151; reached US$922&nbsp;million, an increase
of US$309&nbsp;million when compared to 3Q10. The depreciation of fertilizer assets was US$120&nbsp;million,
an increase of US$83&nbsp;million against 3Q10, due to the impact of the detailing of property and
equipment price allocation. The remaining US$226&nbsp;million can be explained mainly by the ramp up of
Canadian operations, which increased depreciation by US$194&nbsp;million in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Other operational costs reached US$1.193&nbsp;billion, in line with US$1.198&nbsp;billion in 3Q10. The
allocation of the operational costs, other than depreciation and amortization, of Vale
Fertilizantes was US$441&nbsp;million at the same level as US$440&nbsp;million in 3Q10 and which were
accounted in other operational costs until 2010. Going forward the fertilizer operational costs
will be accounted for in COGS.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, demurrage costs &#151; fines paid for delays in loading ships at our maritime terminals
&#151; totaled US$82&nbsp;million, equivalent to US$1.16 per metric ton of iron ore shipped, against US$86
million in the previous quarter.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->13<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="center" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Sales, general and administrative expenses (SG&#038;A) totaled US$647&nbsp;million in 4Q10, US$229&nbsp;million
above 3Q10. The higher SG&#038;A expenses are primarily explained by the increase in consulting services
(US$42&nbsp;million) followed by higher advertising and publicity expenses (US$33&nbsp;million), larger
expenses with personnel (US$27&nbsp;million).
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Research and development (R&#038;D), which reflects our investment in creating long-term growth
opportunities,<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"> </SUP>amounted to US$301&nbsp;million in the quarter, US$85&nbsp;million higher than
3Q10<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">3</SUP>.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Other operational expenses reached US$774&nbsp;million, against US$519&nbsp;million in 3Q10, mostly due to
increased operating levels and non-cash provisions. Pre operating and idle capacity/stoppage
related expenses were US$471&nbsp;million, against US$160&nbsp;million in 3Q10. The increase reflected
start-up expenses of US$277&nbsp;million (mainly due to VNC) and pre- operating costs of US$186&nbsp;million
(related to Moatize, Salobo and On&#231;a Puma). Since we are ramping up VNC with a goal to produce
nickel oxide and simultaneously producing and selling an intermediary product, nickel hydroxide
cake (NHC), the disbursements of VNC impacted both the COGS, for the costs associated to the
production of NHC, and the normal pre-operating expenses.
</DIV>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">





<DIV align="center">

    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="center" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>OPERATING INCOME</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, operating income, as measured by adjusted EBIT, reached a new record of US$21.695
billion, 38.2% higher than the previous record of US$15.698&nbsp;billion in 2008. Operating margin was
47.9% for 2010, 600 basis points greater than 2008.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, operating income was US$7.167&nbsp;billion, decreasing from the US$7.836&nbsp;billion in 3Q10. The
adjusted EBIT margin was 48.0% in 4Q10 versus 55.6% in 3Q10. The main reasons for the decrease of
US$669&nbsp;million were lower iron ore and pellets sales prices (US$658&nbsp;million), higher COGS (US$927
million) and expenses (US$569&nbsp;million). Higher volumes sold of bulk materials (US$343&nbsp;million) and
base metals higher volumes (US$714&nbsp;million) and prices (US$386&nbsp;million) contributed to reduce those
negative effects.
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>NET EARNINGS</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Net earnings reached an all-time high in 2010, at US$17.264&nbsp;billion. They were 30.6% higher
than the previous record of US$13.218&nbsp;billion in 2008, and equal to US$3.25 per share on a fully
diluted basis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, net earnings totaled US$5.917&nbsp;billion, the highest net earnings in a 4Q recorded by Vale,
but slightly below the US$6.038&nbsp;billion in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Financial revenues increased to US$117&nbsp;million from US$56&nbsp;million in the previous quarter.
Financial expenses totaled US$926&nbsp;million, against US$741&nbsp;million in 3Q10 mainly explained by the
mark-to-market of shareholders&#146; debentures, which had meant a non-cash charge of US$276&nbsp;million,
due to rise in its prices.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, the net effect of the mark-to-market of the transactions with derivatives had a positive
impact on earnings of US$473&nbsp;million compared to US$500&nbsp;million in 3Q10. These transactions
produced a net positive cash flow impact of US$1.005&nbsp;billion against only US$97&nbsp;million in the
preceding quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The net result of the currency and interest rate swaps, structured mainly to convert the
BRL-denominated debt into US dollar to protect our cash flow from exchange rate volatility,
produced a positive non-cash effect of US$468&nbsp;million in 4Q10 and a positive cash flow impact of
US$1.045&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our positions with nickel derivatives produced a negative non-cash charge of US$2&nbsp;million in 4Q10
against net earnings and a negative impact of US$38&nbsp;million to our cash flow.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The derivative transactions related to bunker oil and freight costs, structured to minimize the
volatility of the cost of maritime freight from Brazil to Asia, had a positive non-cash effect of
US$17&nbsp;million, and generated a positive impact of US$18&nbsp;million in our cash flow.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">As a consequence of the appreciation of Vale&#146;s functional currency, the Brazilian real, against the
US dollar<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">4</SUP>, foreign exchange and monetary variations caused a positive impact
on our net earnings of US$51&nbsp;million in 4Q10, against US$257&nbsp;million in the previous quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Equity income totaled US$303&nbsp;million in 4Q10, in line with US$305&nbsp;million in 3Q10. The
non-consolidated affiliates in the bulk materials business were the major contributors with US$398
million and logistics with US$32&nbsp;million. These were partly offset by the negative effect of the
equity income from the affiliated steel companies, US$76&nbsp;million, base metals, US$5&nbsp;million and
others, US$46&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Individually, the greatest contributors to equity income were Samarco (US$261&nbsp;million), Longyu
(US$64&nbsp;million) and Hispanobr&#225;s (US$35&nbsp;million).
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 10pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">4</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">From the beginning to the end of the 4Q10
period, the Brazilian real appreciated 1.7% against the US dollar.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->15<!-- /Folio -->

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>CASH GENERATION</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our operations set a record cash generation, as measured by adjusted EBITDA, of US$26.116
billion in 2010. It was 37.3% above the highest mark so far, US$19.018&nbsp;billion in 2008.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, Vale&#146;s adjusted EBITDA also reached a new high of US$8.869&nbsp;billion, compared to US$8.815
billion in 3Q10, our previous record.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Dividends received from non-consolidated affiliates increased to US$629&nbsp;million in 4Q10 from US$283
million in 3Q10 and the major contributors were Samarco (US$575&nbsp;million) and MRS (US$37&nbsp;million).
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The share of bulk materials dropped to 89.8% from 94.6% in 3Q10, while the participation of base
metals almost doubled, rising to 11.0% from 5.9%, due to the increase in prices and volumes sold.
Operations of fertilizers contributed with 1.0%, and logistics with 0.6%. R&#038;D expenditures and
other businesses reduced adjusted EBITDA by 2.4%.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>INVESTMENTS</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>Organic growth</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale invested US$5.091&nbsp;billion, excluding acquisitions, in 4Q10. Capital expenditure in organic
growth totaled US$3.434&nbsp;billion, out of which US$3.103&nbsp;billion was dedicated to project execution,
US$332&nbsp;million to research and development (R&#038;D) and US$1.657&nbsp;billion to the maintenance of
existing operations.
</DIV>



<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->16<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">



<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="30%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="30%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="30%"></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom"><!-- Blank Space -->
    <TD align="left" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="center" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="center" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">R&#038;D investments before adjustments were US$466&nbsp;million in 4Q10, being comprised of US$152
million spent in mineral exploration, US$33&nbsp;million in natural gas exploration, US$241&nbsp;million in
conceptual, pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, and US$40&nbsp;million to develop new processes,
technological innovations
and adaptation of technologies. Part of the expenditures related to the
natural gas exploration program was activated, following the usual approach for the oil and gas
industry, and as a consequence, US$134&nbsp;million of investments in natural gas exploration in 2010
were reclassified from R&#038;D to project execution. After the adjustment, investments in R&#038;D amounted
to US$332&nbsp;million, with US$51&nbsp;million in mineral exploration, in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Investments &#151; excluding acquisitions &#151; in 2010 reached US$12.705&nbsp;billion, with US$8.239&nbsp;billion
allocated to the development of projects, US$1.136&nbsp;billion to R&#038;D &#151; after adjustments in natural
gas exploration &#151; and US$3.330&nbsp;billion to stay-in-business. Investments in corporate social
responsibility reached US$1.136&nbsp;billion, US$737&nbsp;million of which destined for environmental
protection and US$399&nbsp;million for social projects.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">99% of the budgeted capital expenditures for 2010 of US$12.894&nbsp;billion were disbursed. The
adherence of capex execution to the plans was shown also in previous years, such as 2009, when
actual expenditures were 99.7% of budgeted expenditures of US$9.035&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Investments in project execution were 95% of the US$8.647&nbsp;billion budgeted for 2010 and we reached
93% of the US$1.228&nbsp;billion budgeted for research and development (R&#038;D) expenses. This was
partially offset by higher investments in the maintenance of existing operations, mainly driven by
the acquisition of fertilizer assets in Brazil.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, we continued to develop organic growth opportunities through the implementation of
world-class projects. Vale delivered six projects in the year: (a)&nbsp;Additional 20 Mtpy, a low-cost
high-quality iron ore brownfield project at Caraj&#225;s; (b)&nbsp;Bay&#243;var, a phosphate rock mine in Peru;
(c)&nbsp;On&#231;a Puma, a ferronickel operation in the state of Par&#225;, Brazil; (d)&nbsp;Tres Valles, a copper
operation in Chile; (e)&nbsp;Oman, a pellet plant operation in the Middle East; and (f)&nbsp;TKCSA, a steel
slab plant in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">At the end of 1Q10, we started operating new facilities that added 20&nbsp;million metric tons per year
to the capacity of our Caraj&#225;s iron ore mining operations. Due to debottlenecking and the
development of operational flexibility, we were able to double the size of the capacity increase
from our original plans.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the beginning of the third quarter of 2010, we started ramping up operations at Bay&#243;var, a
phosphate rock mine in Peru, with the capacity to produce 3.9&nbsp;million metric tons per year.
Bay&#243;var came on stream on time and on budget and is one of the lowest-cost phosphate rock mines in
the world. It was our first greenfield project in the fertilizer business and also our first
greenfield mining project concluded outside Brazil.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The Oman operations, in the industrial site of Sohar, Oman, are coming on stream. It has two
pellets plants, each with a capacity to produce 4.5 Mtpy, thus adding 9.0 Mtpy to our production
capacity. The two plants will produce direct reduction pellets. Oman&#146;s first plant is under
commissioning and furnace heating, and is expected to start up production in March. The second
plant is being assembled and is expected to reach the ramp up stage by the end of the first half of
this year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the fourth quarter, the Tres Valles copper project in Salamanca, in the Coquimbo region of
Chile, started operations. It includes two mines, Don Gabriel, open pit, and Papomono, underground,
which feed a SXEW (solvent extraction electro winning) plant to produce copper cathodes, with a
capacity of 18,500 metric tons.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Also in the fourth quarter of 2010, we commissioned On&#231;a Puma, a nickel operation (mine and
processing plant) in the Brazilian state of Par&#225;. Its nominal production capacity is 53,000 metric
tons per year of nickel contained in ferronickel, its final product.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Thyssen-Krupp Companhia Sider&#250;rgica do Atl&#226;ntico (TKCSA)&nbsp;began operations in 2010. The plant has
capacity of 5&nbsp;million metric tons per year. Vale has a 26.87% stake and is the exclusive supplier
of iron ore and pellets, around 8.5 Mt of iron ore and pellets per year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In February&nbsp;2011, as part of commitments related to the development of Simandou, which will be the
largest integrated iron ore mine and infrastructure project ever developed in Africa, Vale started
the reconstruction of the Conakry-Kankan railroad in Guinea that will be used for passengers and
general cargo transportation.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->17<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Total investments are estimated in US$1&nbsp;billion, which was not included in the capex of
Simandou phase 1, recently approved by the Board. With the railway&#146;s rehabilitation, Vale aims to
contribute to the social and economic development of the West African nation.

    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>Portfolio asset management</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Although our strategic priority is organic growth, management of the asset portfolio has been a
powerful subsidiary source of value creation to Vale shareholders.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, expenditures to fund acquisitions reached US$6.707&nbsp;billion. In a series of transactions
during 2010, we acquired the Brazilian phosphate operations of two companies: Fertilizantes
Fosfatados S.A. &#151; Fosfertil and Vale Fosfatados (formerly Bunge Participa&#231;&#245;es e Investimentos S.A.).
At year-end 2010, we owned
100% of the shares of Vale Fosfatados, and 78.9% of the equity of Fosfertil, representing
99.8% of its common shares and 68.2% of its preferred shares. The total cost of these acquisitions
was US$5.829&nbsp;billion. In January&nbsp;2011, Vale Fosfatados was incorporated into Vale Fertilizantes.
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 10pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR style="font-size: 3pt">
    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">

<TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">5</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">November&nbsp;2010 to January&nbsp;2011.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Expenditures with acquisitions during the year also included: (a)&nbsp;first installment of the
acquisition of a 51% stake in Simandou for US$500&nbsp;million, with the remaining US$2&nbsp;billion payable
upon achievement of certain milestones, (b)&nbsp;SDCN (Sociedade de Desenvolvimento do Corredor Norte
S.A.) in Mozambique for US$21&nbsp;million, (c)&nbsp;the third installment of the concession of Ferrovia
Norte Sul (US$265&nbsp;million) in Brazil, and (d)&nbsp;an additional 24.5% stake in the Belvedere coal
project in Australia (US$92&nbsp;million), increasing our share in the project to 75.5%
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Divestitures in 2010 generated US$890&nbsp;million. During the year the following transactions were
concluded:
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2Q10 we entered into a transaction with Norsk Hydro ASA (Hydro) to transfer our stakes in
aluminum smelting (Albras), alumina refining (Alunorte and CAP) and bauxite mining (Paragominas and
mineral rights) for U$1.4&nbsp;billion in cash over time plus a net debt of US$700&nbsp;million and 22% of
Hydro&#146;s capital. This transaction is expected to have its closing until the end of 1Q11.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In February&nbsp;2011, we invested US$173.5&nbsp;million to acquire the control of Biopalma, in the state of
Par&#225;, Brazil and previously our partner in a consortium &#151; now dissolved &#151; to invest in biofuels.
Biopalma will produce palm oil, a raw material used to make biodiesel, and most of the production
will be used for the B20 mix (a blend of 20% biodiesel and 80% regular diesel) to power our fleet
of locomotives, heavy-duty machinery and equipment. Our investment in producing biodiesel is part
of the strategic priority to be a global sustainability agent.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><I>For more details about the projects and capex budget for 2011, please see the press release &#147;Vale
to invest US$24&nbsp;billion in 2011&#148;</I>

<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>
<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>DEBT INDICATORS</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Total debt was US$25.343&nbsp;billion as of December&nbsp;31, 2010, with a long average maturity, of 9.6
years. This is important for the minimization of refinancing risks. The recent financial stress in
the peripheral economies of the Euro zone, in which the concentration of maturing debt to be rolled
in a short period of time has played a key role, is a good example of how important it is to
derisking a portfolio of long-term debt.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The average debt cost was 4.85% per year, consistent with the focus on minimization of the cost of
capital. As of December&nbsp;31, 2010, cash holdings reached US$9,377&nbsp;billion, and net
debt<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">(c)</SUP> was US$15.966&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Debt leverage, as measured by total debt/LTM adjusted EBITDA<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">(d)</SUP> ratio, fell to 1.0x on
December&nbsp;31, 2010 from 1.3x on September&nbsp;30, 2010 and 2.5x on December&nbsp;31, 2009, when the negative
effects of the global recession were still impacting our cash flow. The total debt/enterprise
value<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">(e)</SUP> ratio fell to 13.2% on December&nbsp;31, 2010 from 14.4% on September&nbsp;30, 2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Interest coverage, measured by the LTM adjusted EBITDA/LTM interest payment ratio<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">(f)</SUP>,
was 23.8x compared to 18.1x on September&nbsp;30, 2010 and 8.2x in December&nbsp;31, 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Considering hedge positions, the total debt in December&nbsp;2010 was composed of 33% of floating
interest rates and 67% of fixed interest rates linked debt, while 96% was denominated in US dollars
and the remainder in other currencies.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In March&nbsp;2010, Vale made its debut in the Euro debt market by raising &#128;750&nbsp;million through the
issuance of 8-year notes with a coupon of 4.375%, paid annually.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In September&nbsp;2010, we raised US$1.75&nbsp;billion through the issuance of US$1&nbsp;billion notes due
2020@4.625% per annum, payable semi-annually, and US$750&nbsp;million notes due 2039@6.875% per annum,
payable semi-annually and yield to investors of 6.074%. The 2039 notes are consolidated in a form
of single series with the US$1&nbsp;billion notes 2039 issued in November&nbsp;2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">We have entered into agreements with official credit institutions of different countries &#151; Brazil,
Japan, Korea, China and Canada &#151; for credit lines with terms and costs conditions proper to the
financing of mining and infrastructure projects. In February&nbsp;2011 we signed a contract with Servizi
Assicurativi Del Commercio Estero Spa. (SACE), an official credit agency from Italy, to guarantee a
10-year credit line of US$300&nbsp;million provided by commercial banks.
</DIV>
