<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>



<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, the shipments of iron ore amounted to 254.902&nbsp;million metric tons, 3.4% below the record
sales volume in 2008. Shipment of pellets totaled 39.512&nbsp;million metric tons in 2010, the highest
level in Vale&#146;s history, surpassing the all-time high figure of 33.670&nbsp;million reached in 2007.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Revenues from iron ore sales reached an all-time high, at US$26.383&nbsp;billion in 2010, being 48.4%
above the value of US$17.775&nbsp;billion for 2008, a peak until then. By the same token, revenues from
pellet shipments set a record, at US$6.373&nbsp;billion, surpassing the prior record mark of US$4.245
billion in 2008 by 50.1%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The performance of iron ore and pellet prices during the year, reflecting disequilibrium between
global demand and supply, was the main cause for the significant growth in revenues. The new iron
ore pricing system implemented by Vale brought several benefits to market participants, including
flexibility, efficiency in price discovery, transparency and rewarding of superior quality, a
hallmark of our products. In addition to the contribution to our performance, the new system is
issuing the right signals, one of the most important roles played by market price mechanisms. These
signals are leading us to invest a major amount of resources in the development of high quality
production capacity to satisfy the needs of a modern global steel industry.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, volumes of iron ore and pellets shipments were 80.541&nbsp;million metric tons, an increase of
2.4% compared to 3Q10, being the best sales performance of iron ore and pellets in Vale&#146;s history
in a 4Q. Sales volumes of iron ore totaled 69.860&nbsp;million metric tons, 2.7% higher that 3Q10, and
pellets sales accounted for 10.681&nbsp;million metric tons, slightly above the 10.585&nbsp;million metric
tons in the 3Q10, and a record high in Vale&#146;s history.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Sales revenues from iron ore and pellets, in 4Q10, totaled US$10.394&nbsp;billion, 3.8% less than the
previous quarter, due to lower realized prices. Sales of iron ore and pellets were US$8.476&nbsp;billion
and US$1.918&nbsp;billion, respectively, decreasing of 2.8% and 7.6% relative to 3Q10, respectively. In
4Q10, the average realized price of iron ore was US$121.34 per metric ton, 5.4% lower than 3Q10.
Average pellet price was US$179.53 per metric ton, 8.5% lower than 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Even increasing significantly capacity utilization of our iron ore operations, we were forced to
reduce shipments to China, to 126.400 Mt from 140.396 Mt in 2009 in order to give room to
satisfying the demand recovery in other markets, particularly in Brazil and Europe, where our
shipments increased by 15.058 Mt and 27.735 Mt, respectively. Thereby, China&#146;s share in our sales
of iron ore and pellets decreased to 42.9% in 2010 from 56.8% in 2009, while Europe&#146;s share
increased to 20.7% from 13.4% in 2009, recovering some of the ground lost with the recession.
Brazil accounted for 13.7% of volumes sold, from 10.2% in 2009, and Japan represented 10.5%, from
9.1% in the previous year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">It is worthwhile noting that reported revenues for iron ore and pellets are net of the costs of
maritime freight, meaning that prices of cost and freight (CFR)&nbsp;sales are comparable to average FOB
prices. In 4Q10, Vale sold 31.3&nbsp;million metric tons of iron ore and pellets on a CFR basis, against
25.0&nbsp;million metric tons in 3Q10. In 2010, sales volume of iron ore and pellets on a CFR basis
amounted to 81.9&nbsp;million metric tons.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, shipments of manganese ore reached 1.119 Mt, 47.4% above 2008, and sales volumes of
ferroalloys totaled 401,000 metric tons, in line with the 396,000 metric tons reached in 2008.
Manganese ore revenues amounted to US$258&nbsp;million, while those originated from ferroalloys totaled
US$621&nbsp;million, lower than US$1.073&nbsp;billion in 2008, when their prices peaked.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, sales volumes of manganese ore were 352,000 metric tons, 51.1% higher than 3Q10, and
revenues were US$44&nbsp;million, 34.0% lower than 3Q10, due to lower realized prices of US$125.00 in
the quarter. Sales volumes of ferroalloys were 109,000 metric tons in 4Q10, 21.1% higher than the
previous quarter and sales revenues were US$170&nbsp;million, 6.5% higher than 3Q10, with the average
realized prices of US$1,559.63 per metric ton in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Gross revenues from ferrous minerals &#151; iron ore, pellets, manganese and ferroalloys&#151; were
US$33.739&nbsp;billion in 2010, reaching all time high level in Vale&#146;s history, being 42.4% above the
previous record of 2008. In 4Q10, gross revenues from ferrous minerals totaled US$10.656&nbsp;billion,
3.5% lower than 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The adjusted EBIT margin for the ferrous minerals business was 65.7% in 4Q10, compared to 70.3% in
3Q10. In 2010, the operational margin was 64.3%, higher than 54.1% in 2008.
</DIV>
<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->21<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Adjusted EBITDA for the ferrous minerals operations totaled US$7.978&nbsp;billion in 4Q10, dropping 3.5%
on a quarter-on-quarter basis. The decrease of US$286&nbsp;million was mainly due lower sales prices,
which had a negative impact of US$670&nbsp;million on the cash flow, and was partly offset by higher
sales volumes, with a contribution of US$245&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, adjusted EBITDA reached US$23.976&nbsp;billion, a record figure, 72.7% higher than the previous
record in 2008.
</DIV>

<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->

<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B><I>Coal</I></B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Revenues from sales of coal products reached a record of US$241&nbsp;million in 4Q10, with a
quarter-on-quarter increase of 11.3%. In 4Q10, revenues from shipments of metallurgical coal were
US$191&nbsp;million, increasing 82.7% on a quarterly basis. But, on the other hand, thermal coal
revenues were US$51&nbsp;million versus US$113&nbsp;million in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The total revenue of US$770&nbsp;million in 2010 &#151; a record figure &#151; increased 52.6% vis-&#224;-vis 2009.
The better performance was mainly due to the higher volume sold of thermal and metallurgical coal,
reaching 7,384,000 metric tons from 5,673,000 metric tons in 2009 and 4,087,000 metric tons in
2008.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The average sale price of metallurgical coal in 4Q10 was US$172.33 per metric ton, 6.7% lower than
3Q10, and US$63.96 per metric ton for thermal coal against US$98.73 per metric ton in the previous
quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Adjusted EBITDA for the coal business was negative by US$15&nbsp;million in 4Q10, a decrease of US$87
million from 3Q10, mainly due to the increase in SG&#038;A expenses by US$74&nbsp;million. In 2010, adjusted
EBITDA totaled US$21&nbsp;million, against negative US$1&nbsp;million in 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>Base metals</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Shipments of nickel and its by-products, copper, cobalt and PGMs &#151; were negatively affected by
the strike in our Canadian operations in Sudbury, Port Colborne and Voisey&#146;s Bay. On the other
hand, prices have recovered in 2010, after falling in 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Revenues from shipments of base metals recovered in 2010, reaching US$8.2&nbsp;billion, with a
year-on-year increase of 22.8%. With the return to normalcy of the Canadian operations in 4Q10,
there was a sharp improvement in the sales revenues, which climbed to US$3.019&nbsp;billion, increasing
57.3% over 3Q10.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->23<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>



<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#C13242tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; margin-left: .25in; width: 7.50in">

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top"><B><I>US GAAP</I></B>
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top"><B><I>4Q10</I></B></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, nickel revenues reached US$1.437&nbsp;billion, 61.2% higher than 3Q10 when it was US$891
million. This increase of US$546&nbsp;million is due to both higher volumes, US$456&nbsp;million, and prices,
US$90&nbsp;million. Sales volumes in 4Q10 were 63,000 metric tons, against 42,000 in 3Q10. The average
nickel price in 4Q10 was slightly higher, US$22,955 per metric ton in 4Q10 versus US$21,366 in the
previous quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Copper revenues amounted to US$753&nbsp;million in 4Q10, up 90.7% compared to US$395&nbsp;million in 3Q10.
Shipments reached 82,000 metric tons in 4Q10, 49.3% higher than the volume of 3Q10. In 4Q10, the
average copper price increased to US$9,134 per metric ton from US$7,153 in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, PGMs produced revenues of US$77&nbsp;million from US$10&nbsp;million in 3Q10, influenced by the
higher average platinum price in 4Q10, US$1,674 per troy ounce, over US$1,552 per troy ounce in the
previous quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Revenues from sales of bauxite, alumina and aluminum amounted US$691&nbsp;million in 4Q10 up 13.5% from
3Q10 due to increase in sales prices.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The average sales price of aluminum was US$2,246 per metric ton in 4Q10 against US$1,990 per metric
ton in 3Q10, while the price of alumina, which is mostly indexed to the metal price, increased to
US$295.47 per metric ton in this quarter from US$272.15 per metric ton in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, shipments of aluminum were 130,000 metric tons, compared with 97,000 metric tons in 3Q10.
Sales of alumina amounted to 1.303&nbsp;million metric tons versus 1.422&nbsp;million metric tons in the
previous quarter. Bauxite volume increased to 296,000 metric tons against 204,000 metric tons in
3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The adjusted EBIT margin of the base metals increased to 12.6% in 4Q10, from 11.7% in 3Q10. In
2010, operational margin was 8.0%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Adjusted EBITDA surged to US$978&nbsp;million in 4Q10, increasing 87.7% against 3Q10. The increase was
mainly due to higher sales volumes (US$454&nbsp;million) and higher sales prices (US$394&nbsp;million) which
were partly offset by an increase in SG&#038;A expenses (US$195&nbsp;million) and in COGS (US$181&nbsp;million).
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, adjusted EBITDA totaled US$2.294&nbsp;billion, almost twice the figure for 2009, US$1.159
billion.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>Fertilizer nutrients</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Total revenues from fertilizer nutrients were US$769&nbsp;million in 4Q10, slightly less than the
US$801&nbsp;million for 3Q10. In 2010, sales revenues totaled US$1.846&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, potash produced revenues of US$74&nbsp;million, with a quarter-on-quarter decrease of 14.9%.
Sales volumes were 174,000 metric tons in 4Q10, down from 217,000 metric tons in 3Q10. The average
sales prices increased to US$425.29, 6.1% higher than 3Q10, partly mitigating the effect of lower
volume sales on revenues. In 2010, revenues from potash sales totaled US$280&nbsp;million, 32.2% less
than in 2009. The decrease of US$133&nbsp;million from 2009 was due to diminished prices and sales
volumes, with a negative impact of US$76&nbsp;million and US$57&nbsp;million, respectively.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Revenues from sales of phosphates products were US$512&nbsp;million in 4Q10, 10.6% lower than 3Q10.
Total shipments of MAP were 305,000 metric tons (t), TSP 113,000 t, SSP 547,000 t, and DCP 114,000
t.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Sales of nitrogen fertilizers increased to US$178&nbsp;million in 4Q10, 35.4% higher on a quarterly
basis. Sales of other related products amounted to US$5&nbsp;million in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The EBIT margin of the fertilizer nutrients business was -11.0% in 4Q10, against -2.0% in 3Q10. The
main reason for the negative operating margin was the impact of the depreciation charges, which
resulted from the fair value inventory adjustment of acquired fertilizer assets. If this effect of
US$99&nbsp;million &#151; a non-recurring non-cash charge &#151; was excluded, the operating margin would have
been of 2.4%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Adjusted EBITDA for the fertilizers business totaled US$86&nbsp;million in 4Q10, 59.3% higher than 3Q10.
Lower COGS made a positive contribution to cash generation of US$103&nbsp;million, but higher SG&#038;A had a
negative impact of US$39&nbsp;million. In 2010, adjusted EBITDA totaled US$176&nbsp;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 10pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify"><B>Logistics services</B></DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Logistics services produced revenues of US$1.460&nbsp;billion in 2010, 32.5% greater than in 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, revenues were US$335&nbsp;million, dropping US$72&nbsp;million from the US$407&nbsp;million earned in
3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Due to lower volumes of services, revenues from rail transportation of general cargo of US$262
million fell US$46&nbsp;million when compared to the preceding quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale railroads &#151; Caraj&#225;s (EFC), Vit&#243;ria a Minas (EFVM), Norte-Sul (FNS)&nbsp;and Centro-Atl&#226;ntica (FCA)
&#151; transported 5.790&nbsp;billion ntk<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">6</SUP> of general cargo for clients in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The main cargoes carried by our railroads in 4Q10 were agricultural products (44.2%), steel
industry inputs and products (36.6%), fuels (8.5%), building materials and forestry products
(2.0%), and others (7.3%).
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Port services revenues reached US$73&nbsp;million in 4Q10, totaling US$353&nbsp;million in 2010. Our ports
and maritime terminals handled 4.579 Mt of general cargo, a volume 34.7% lower than the 7.010 Mt of
3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The demand for transportation of general cargo is seasonally weaker in the fourth quarter due to
the end of the crop season in Brazil. In addition, there was an accident at the Praia Mole maritime
terminal &#151; used to unload coal imports made by the steel industry &#151; caused by very strong winds,
contributing to the loss of revenues. Railroad transportation volumes fell by 16.4% on a
quarter-on-quarter basis, whereas the amount of cargo handled by our maritime terminals dropped by
41.4%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 2010, Vale&#146;s railroads carried 25.283&nbsp;billion ntk, with a 15.7% increase against 2009, and
maritime terminals handled 23.319&nbsp;million tons, increasing 8.6% year-on-year.
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 10pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR style="font-size: 6pt">
    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">6</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Ntk=net ton kilometer</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, adjusted EBIT margin was negative on -5.2%, from 18.2% in 3Q10, due to the large drop
in services sold, some decrease in average prices and a cost increase of US$38&nbsp;million, mainly to
higher spending with personnel.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Adjusted EBITDA for the logistics business was US$56&nbsp;million in 4Q10, 51.7% lower than the previous
quarter, mainly due to higher COGS, US$46&nbsp;million, and lower transported volume, US$33&nbsp;million. In
2010, adjusted EBITDA totaled US$ 345&nbsp;million.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>IFRS &#151; RECONCILIATION WITH USGAAP</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Since December&nbsp;2007, significant modifications have been made to Brazilian GAAP as part of a
Convergence project with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). By the end of 2010,
the convergence of the full year financial statements will be completed and therefore the IFRS will
be the accounting standard adopted in Brazil. During the intermediate periods of 2010, we already
adopted all pronouncements issued by the Brazilian Accounting Practice Committee (CPC)&nbsp;which are in
conformity with the IFRS.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The net income reconciliation between the 4Q10 net income according to Brazilian rules (in
conformity with the IFRS) and USGAAP is as follows:
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Depletion of assets on business acquired: </B>Refers to additional depletion of the adjustments to
fair value of property, plant and equipment on business acquired before the new rules issued by CPC
in respect of business combinations. This difference will cease by the end of the useful life of
these assets.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Pension Plan: </B>This adjustment reflects the return on the overfunded plans, which under IFRS are
only recorded if there is a clear evidence of their realization.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Other adjustments: </B>Refers basically to the adjustment to present value of interest on mandatorily
convertible notes due to the bifurcation approach.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Income tax: </B>Income tax related to the previously described adjustments.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>(b)&nbsp;Adjusted EBITDA</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">EBITDA defines profit or loss before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. Vale uses the term adjusted EBITDA to reflect exclusion, also, of: monetary
variations; equity income from the profit or loss of affiliated companies and joint ventures, less the dividends received from them; provisions for losses on
investments; adjustments for changes in accounting practices; minority interests; and non-recurrent expenses. However our adjusted EBITDA is not the measure defined
as EBITDA under US GAAP, and may possibly not be comparable with indicators with the same name reported by other companies. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered
as a substitute for operational profit or as a better measure of liquidity than operational cash flow, which are calculated in accordance with GAAP. Vale provides
its adjusted EBITDA to give additional information about its capacity to pay debt, carry out investments and cover working capital needs. The following table shows
the reconciliation between adjusted EBITDA and operational cash flow, in accordance with its statement of changes in financial position:
</DIV>
